context: Field extensions: algebraic extension that is an algebraically closed field

formulations.text: Given a field F, an algebraic closure of F is an extension field K containing F in which every element is algebraic over F and every nonconstant polynomial over K has a root in K.
formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.

context: Field theory: no nontrivial algebraic field extensions

formulations.text: A field K is algebraically closed precisely when it has no proper algebraic field extension; equivalently, each nonconstant one-variable polynomial with coefficients in K admits a root in K.
formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.

formulations.text: A field F is algebraically closed exactly when every polynomial in F[x] of positive degree has at least one zero in F.
formulations.equivalence_note: Equivalent polynomial-root characterization to the no-proper-algebraic-extension formulation (Stacks Lemma 9.10.2).

context: Topology: basis consisting of open sets

formulations.text: For a topological space X, a basis is a family B of open sets such that, whenever an open U contains x, some member of B contains x and is itself contained in U.
formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.

context: Topology: subbasis whose finite intersections are a basis

formulations.text: A subbasis for an existing topology on X is a family of open subsets whose finite intersections form a basis for that topology, with the empty intersection taken as X.
formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.

context: Algebraic geometry: spectrum as a locally ringed space

formulations.text: An affine scheme is a locally ringed space isomorphic to the prime spectrum of a commutative ring equipped with its structure sheaf.
formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.

formulations.text: In a category C, an object I is initial if every object Y of C is the target of exactly one morphism originating at I.
formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.

formulations.text: In a category C, an object T is terminal (final) if for every object Y of C there is exactly one morphism from Y to T.
formulations.editorial_note: Cross-checked against cited Stacks section; independent paraphrase, not independently human-verified.

context: Set theory: initial ordinal of a well-orderable set

formulations.text: For a set A, its cardinality may be represented by the smallest ordinal equipotent to A, meaning the least ordinal for which a bijection with A exists.
